parameters.label: ^c20260814-12u
parameters.text: `Chatlas2.System` is the parallel experimental system in which the new Chatlas model can mature without constraining current Chatlas.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-13u
parameters.text: Chatlas2 may depend on current Chatlas code; current Chatlas must not depend on Chatlas2 code.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-14u
parameters.text: Chatlas mechanics may be reused freely, while inherited semantic judgments are reviewed and may be redesigned or reimplemented.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-15u
parameters.text: The existing lossless `Raw.Archive`, safe provider discovery and capture, and session identity primitives remain available to Chatlas2.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-16u
parameters.text: Chatlas2 keeps its CPU implementation deliberately simple; agents may inspect the retained raw artifacts when they need resolution beyond the Normal Model.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-16u
parameters.text: `Chatlas2.Normal.Model` is a provider-neutral, loss-preserving chronological event tape with a deliberately shallow semantic floor.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-17u
parameters.text: Normalization reviews every retained artifact or independently parseable fragment that may contain otherwise-lost session data; no primary artifact decides what survives.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-18u
parameters.text: Deduplication fails toward retention: observations are collapsed only when they can be shown to describe the same event; uncertainty preserves both.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-19u
parameters.text: An event's tape timetag is when the event starts; later observations may add data to that event without changing its start position.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-20u
parameters.text: Data completeness has priority over total consistency; richer semantic resolution can be added later without discarding the retained event data.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-72u
parameters.text: `Normal.Model.Cache` is a disposable materialization of a completed compact `Chatlas2.Normal.Model` for efficient repeated reading.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-74u
parameters.text: A `Raw.Normalizer` may use any internal strategy it needs to produce a complete Normal Model; cache and read-streaming mechanics do not constrain normalization.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-75u
parameters.text: Streaming is a read-side property of a completed cached Normal Model, not a production requirement imposed on normalizers.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-49u
parameters.text: The cache representation is one metadata record plus independently stream-readable line-delimited collections for events, `Chat.Message`, `Chat.Turn`, and `Agent.Loaded.Context`.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-51u
parameters.text: The message collection retains parsed transcript content, while the turn collection stays compact by retaining the refs of its mostly opaque member events.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-52u
parameters.text: A full turn read hydrates associated opaque information on demand through the turn's event refs instead of duplicating that information in the compact turn collection.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-77u
parameters.text: Cache identity and freshness are determined from session identity, ordered source fingerprints, Normal Model schema, and producing commit.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-78u
parameters.text: A Normal Model cache is disposable and non-authoritative; it can be rebuilt from the retained Raw Archive.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-29u
parameters.text: Ordinary caches contain the compact default Normal Model; raw-attached diagnostic builds are not retained as ordinary caches.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-30u
parameters.text: A bulk read never silently normalizes missing or stale caches.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-31u
parameters.text: Cache creation is explicit, except that a narrowly scoped read of one exact session may build that session's cache.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-32u
parameters.text: A multi-session workflow opens, consumes, and releases one Normal Model at a time instead of retaining a collection of loaded models.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-33u
parameters.text: Read limits and top-K selection are applied while streaming cached collections so unrelated records need not be materialized.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-34u
parameters.text: Read-side caching does not remove the first-build memory peak; the normalizer remains responsible for its own creation strategy.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-36u
parameters.text: The canonical Normal Model provider is the default consumer boundary: it transparently validates and reuses a fresh cache or rebuilds a missing/stale one.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-36u~2
parameters.text: Explicit refresh forces compact recomputation and cache replacement; raw-attached diagnostic computation bypasses the ordinary cache.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-36u~3
parameters.text: Consumers request complete or stream-readable Normal Model content and own no cache validation or recomputation policy; Anchory is one ordinary complete-model consumer.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-53u
parameters.text: `Scan.Decode.Verify` is the JSONL read escalation that scans raw line text for candidates, decodes only candidate records, and verifies matches against the parsed object.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-54u
parameters.text: A textual scan may admit false-positive candidates but must not exclude a record that could satisfy the promised query.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-55u
parameters.text: Candidate selection escalates from literal byte or string search when sufficient, to compiled regular expressions for broader structural selection, to decoded object checks for semantic truth.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-56u
parameters.text: The parsed record is authoritative for a match, and query limits apply only after parsed verification succeeds.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-57u
parameters.text: When a complete textual candidate predicate cannot be constructed safely, the reader decodes every line rather than risking a false negative.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-39u
parameters.text: Raw is optional normalizer-owned diagnostic material used to produce a Normal Fragment; it is omitted by default and imposes no complete-artifact inspection contract.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-61u
parameters.text: Raw evidence is independent from the Normal Model's event identity, ordering, annotations, and reference standing.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-21u
parameters.text: `Raw.Model.Versioner` inspects raw structure and content, returns one stable Chatlas-assigned `Raw.Model.Version` or null, and performs no semantic normalization.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-59u
parameters.text: `Raw.Model.Version` partitions raw fragments by compatible mapping structure so each supported `Raw.Normalizer` can keep its raw-to-normal mapping direct and simple.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-67u
parameters.text: `Raw.Model.Version` identifiers are opaque arbitrary names; their spelling carries no ordering, compatibility, or succession semantics.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-22u
parameters.text: Provider or CLI versions may inform recognition but never define `Raw.Model.Version` by themselves.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-23u
parameters.text: A `Raw.Normalizer` declares exactly which `Raw.Model.Version` values it supports and runs only after successful version recognition.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-24u
parameters.text: Recognition and normalization operate on the smallest independently parseable raw fragment, allowing one session to contain several raw model versions.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-60u
parameters.text: Within one coherent Normal Model design lineage, evolution may preserve, extend, or refine existing `Raw.Model.Version` partitions when new mappings expose previously irrelevant raw differences.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-61u
parameters.text: Incremental Normal Model evolution does not introduce a raw-version axis unrelated to the existing compatible-mapping partition.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-62u
parameters.text: A full Normal Model redesign may establish a new `Raw.Model.Version` partition because the applicable notion of compatible mapping has changed.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-63u
parameters.text: A prior raw-version partition remains valid for the Normal Model design lineage that assigned it rather than becoming retroactively wrong.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-54u
parameters.text: One `Raw.Model.Version` may include declared optional fields when important data remains at the same raw paths with the same meaning.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-55u
parameters.text: Normalizer simplicity is versioning pressure: alternative raw path maps, schema-era checks, or substantial fallback branching usually indicate distinct `Raw.Model.Version` values.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-56u
parameters.text: Normalizers for different `Raw.Model.Version` values may share readers, validators, and event-building machinery while keeping each version's raw-path mapping direct.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-57u
parameters.text: Moving an important datum from raw path A to raw path B is evidence for a new `Raw.Model.Version` even when both adapters map it to the same Normal Model path A'.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-58u
parameters.text: `Raw.Model.Versioner` implementations may expand recognition coverage without changing the structural meaning of an existing `Raw.Model.Version`.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-64u
parameters.text: `Raw.Model.Version` is dispatch and provenance metadata; it does not participate in stable `Event.Address` or `Chat.Message.Address` identity.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-26u
parameters.text: Normal Model metadata records the producing repository's last Git commit under the future-proof field name `commit`; no stronger reproducibility model is required initially.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-0u
parameters.text: `Chatlas2.Event.Origin` has two resolved structural types, `User.Event` and `Agent.Event`; `Unresolved.Event` is the preservation state when neither side can be asserted safely.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-1u
parameters.text: `Agent.Event` deliberately collapses assistant, model, harness, tool, runtime, compaction, and context distinctions at the structural level.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-2u
parameters.text: Origin is asserted only when the user-side or agent-side boundary can be established; otherwise the event remains unresolved rather than being guessed into a side.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-3u
parameters.text: Chatlas2's main semantic promise is correct user-side versus agent-side classification whenever it claims that distinction.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-4u
parameters.text: `Chat.Message` is an event or event grouping belonging to the primary user-agent message exchange, not everything the harness renders to the user.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-5u
parameters.text: Every `User.Message` is represented over one or more `User.Event` members.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-6u
parameters.text: Every `Agent.Message` is represented over one or more `Agent.Event` members.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-7u
parameters.text: Chatlas2 always provides the complete `User.Message` and `Agent.Message` projection because these are the messages the user sees and reacts to.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-8u
parameters.text: `Chat.Message` membership is modeled as an annotation or grouping over the event tape rather than as another canonical spine.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-42u
parameters.text: `Chat.Turn` is the side-resolved grouping of events associated with one user or agent conversational turn and is the semantic blob boundary for that turn's provider data.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-43u
parameters.text: Every `Chat.Message` belongs to one containing `Chat.Turn`, and the message's member events are a subset of the turn's member events.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-44u
parameters.text: A `Chat.Turn` may contain zero, one, or several `Chat.Message` groupings.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-45u
parameters.text: Chatlas interprets the primary `Chat.Message` text while retaining the turn's other associated events and provider data opaquely rather than independently modeling their semantics.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-46u
parameters.text: An event whose conversational-turn association cannot be established remains chronologically on the event tape without being guessed into a `Chat.Turn`.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-47u
parameters.text: `Chat.Message.Hash` changes with the communicated message text, while `Chat.Turn.Hash` changes when any associated event or opaque payload changes.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-48u
parameters.text: Grounding identifies communicated evidence through `Chat.Message.Ref`; a consumer may expand that message to its containing `Chat.Turn` when it needs the associated opaque information.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-46u
parameters.text: `Chat.Message.Address` is a stable provider-derived logical message place, independent from message content and chronological presentation order.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-46u~2
parameters.text: `Chat.Message.Hash` asserts the message side plus its ordered member `Event.Hash` values.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-46u~3
parameters.text: `Chat.Message.Ref` is `{message_address, message_hash}` and resolves against the current message projection as `MATCHED`, `AMENDED`, or `MISSING`.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-37u
parameters.text: `Chatlas2.Views` is the public disposable read-projection route introduced under `tarav chatlas2 views`; it reads canonical Normal Model content rather than defining another model.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-41u
parameters.text: Hugentic chat-grounding routes use Chatlas2 message-support or line-dossier records, while mixed readers continue to resolve existing current-Chatlas anchors during the experimental cutover.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-17u
parameters.text: `Agent.Loaded.Context` is the grouping of events that normalization determines were available to contextualize a specific generated `Agent.Event`.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-18u
parameters.text: For a generated `Agent.Event`, its `Agent.Loaded.Context` answers which context was used for the corresponding LLM call.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-19u
parameters.text: Membership asserts that an event was available to the LLM call; it does not assert that the agent noticed or used the event.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-20u
parameters.text: Normalization constructs each context grouping from the provider transcript and evidence about how that provider forms its LLM calls.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-21u
parameters.text: Context membership is conservative: an incomplete grouping is preferable to false-positive membership.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-22u
parameters.text: A context grouping may contain most preceding events, but the model imposes no size or prefix constraint on it.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-23u
parameters.text: `Agent.Loaded.Context` does not introduce an `Agent.Execution` concept; it associates directly with the generated `Agent.Event`.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-24u
parameters.text: `Normal.Context.Blob` is not part of the model; `Agent.Loaded.Context` groups the minimally parsed events already retained on the tape.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-37u
parameters.text: `Event.Address` is a stable, opaque, provider-derived logical event place; it excludes event content and chronological presentation position.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-38u
parameters.text: `Event.Hash` is a digest assertion over an event's currently normalized content; it excludes address, annotations, native identifiers, and provenance.

parameters.label: ^c20260816-28u
parameters.text: Event.Hash is deliberately computed from provider-neutral normalized event fields and excludes optional normalizer-collected raw evidence.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-39u
parameters.text: `Event.Ref` is `{event_address, event_hash}`: it couples stable logical place with a current-state assertion and carries drift validation.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-40u
parameters.text: Chatlas2 normalization is stateless: current raw artifacts produce the current Normal Model without maintaining normalized state across runs.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-41u
parameters.text: `Event.Ref.Resolution` is Chatlas's comparison of a stored `Event.Ref` with the currently presented Normal Model.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-42u
parameters.text: `Event.Ref.Resolution` is `MATCHED` when address and hash agree, `AMENDED` when the address exists with a different current hash, and `MISSING` when the address is absent.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-43u
parameters.text: Chatlas presents the resolution standing; each consumer decides what policy to apply to it.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-44u
parameters.text: Chatlas2 does not retain earlier normalized event states merely to explain amendments; historical artifact debugging belongs to the Raw Archive's Git history.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-27u
parameters.text: `Chatlas2.Progressive.Resolution` is the optional layer of classes, annotations, and groupings added over preserved events as reliable needs emerge.

parameters.label: ^c20260815-9u
parameters.text: Event classes such as `user.message`, `user.interrupt`, and `agent.message` may be added when their resolution becomes useful and reliable.

parameters.label: ^c20260814-29u
parameters.text: Later resolution enriches the event tape without replacing its retained data, chronological order, or origin assertions.

parameters.text: **Source:** the user requested a Chatlas2-targeted redesign that reuses proven Chatlas update mechanics without inheriting the old read-side escalation complexity.

parameters.label: ^m2208-5555ae87ba7bbf01
parameters.text: `Chatlas2.Update.Preflight` is an explicit CLI boundary: update the retained source material once, then execute the requested command once.

parameters.label: ^m2208-3aa034ab647b9c23
parameters.text: `--update` is a boolean top-level Chatlas2 option, used as `tarav chatlas2 --update ...`; it does not expose Chatlas1's direct/index/recent/full satisfaction ladder.

parameters.label: ^m2208-0e9866a29f446413
parameters.text: The update mutates only Raw.Archive and Session.Index. It never writes a Normal Model directly; the canonical Chatlas2 provider remains responsible for cache freshness and reconstruction.

parameters.label: ^m2208-23b844d443c939fc
parameters.text: The preflight fails closed: when update fails, the selected command does not run and stale output is not presented as freshly updated.

parameters.label: ^m2208-a7c7a5c546b03bb5
parameters.text: Keep the update result off stdout so every existing JSON-producing command preserves its output contract; progress may use stderr.

parameters.label: ^m2208-8c3c68c001ecc0e2
parameters.text: Update scope is derived only from structural CLI selectors, never message text or other content predicates.

parameters.label: ^m2208-40cba4b2f0cd91c8
parameters.text: A native `--session-id` produces one exact-session delta scan over the explicitly selected provider or the two Chatlas2-supported providers.

parameters.label: ^m2208-d3d209ed293e9916
parameters.text: A known `--identity-hash` resolves through Session.Index to the native session and provider before scanning; an unknown identity falls back to the supported provider scope so newly discoverable material is not excluded by stale metadata.

parameters.label: ^m2208-5dea52b3dde05306
parameters.text: A command without an exact selector performs one cached delta scan over its selected provider set, defaulting to Codex and Claude Code.

parameters.label: ^m2208-c3aa171eca5f9677
parameters.text: Do not retry progressively until a non-empty read appears. Empty is a valid result and update policy must not depend on consumer result shape.

parameters.label: ^m2208-f6864a98d72a1141
parameters.text: Reuse the existing Provider.Home adapters, archive copier, derivation signatures, scoped scanner, and Session.Index writer behind `chatlas_update()`.

parameters.label: ^m2208-db8597c18e06c872
parameters.text: Reimplement Chatlas2's orchestration in the Chatlas2 namespace rather than importing the Chatlas1 CLI helper, whose tier ladder and satisfaction predicates are coupled to Chatlas1 commands.

parameters.label: ^m2208-95bc794b10b7bc47
parameters.text: Preserve the dependency direction: Chatlas2 may depend on Chatlas mechanics; Chatlas must not depend on Chatlas2.

parameters.label: ^m2208-6544cde9b7f8962d
parameters.text: This slice can later replace shared archive mechanics behind the same Chatlas2 preflight without changing consumer command semantics.

parameters.text: `Session.Lineage` is the relation model connecting event origins, branches, and continuations within or across `Session.Identity` instances

parameters.label: ^c20260806-112u
parameters.text: each session retains its own linear-chronological `Session.Event.Tape`; lineage edges form the graph projected over those tapes

parameters.label: ^c20260806-113u
parameters.text: an event may reference a prior event as its origin within the same session or across a session boundary

parameters.label: ^c20260806-114u
parameters.text: a compaction-continuation edge connects the session containing the covered history to its continuation through shared `Compaction.Event` evidence

parameters.label: ^c20260806-115u
parameters.text: cross-session lineage is derived only from shared provider evidence such as boundary identifiers, logical parents, or preserved-segment references

parameters.label: ^c20260806-116u
parameters.text: traversable lineage does not merge or duplicate predecessor events into the continuation tape

parameters.label: ^c20260808-37u
parameters.text: every event and `Normal.Turn` on every lineage path remains first-class data in its original `Session.Event.Tape`

parameters.label: ^c20260808-38u
parameters.text: `Session.Lineage` does not classify any event or path as active, current, abandoned, inactive, or default

parameters.label: ^c20260808-39u
parameters.text: lineage relations describe provider-evidenced origins and continuations without assigning status to the resulting paths

parameters.label: ^c20260808-40u
parameters.text: preserving every `Normal.Turn::User.Turn` across branching is a primary requirement of `Session.Lineage`

parameters.label: ^c20260808-42u
parameters.text: consumers may select, rank, or project lineage paths and heads according to their own tasks

parameters.label: ^c20260808-41u
parameters.text: `Lineage.Branch` is the `Session.Lineage` structure formed when multiple event continuations share an earlier event origin

parameters.label: ^c20260808-43u
parameters.text: each continuation relation connects its event to the evidenced origin through an `Event.Ref`

parameters.label: ^c20260808-44u
parameters.text: branch relations are derived only from provider-native lineage evidence

parameters.label: ^c20260808-46u
parameters.text: `Session.Event.Tape` preserves recording chronology while lineage relations project the branching graph over its event places

parameters.label: ^c20260808-47u
parameters.text: creating a branch relation does not invalidate, demote, or change the authority of events on another branch

parameters.label: ^c20260808-45u
parameters.text: continuations `A → B → C` and `A → D` form a branch at `A`; `B`, `C`, and `D` remain equally first-class events

parameters.label: ^c20260807-63u
parameters.text: `Lineage.Rollback` is a provider-evidenced event recording that a continuation resumed from an earlier event origin after later events had already been recorded

parameters.label: ^c20260807-64u
parameters.text: the rollback event occupies its own chronological place on `Session.Event.Tape` and references the evidenced origin

parameters.label: ^c20260807-66u

parameters.label: ^c20260807-65u
parameters.text: rollback does not identify any resulting lineage path as active, current, or preferred

parameters.label: ^c20260807-68u
parameters.text: implicit branching without provider evidence of a rollback operation is represented through `Lineage.Branch`, not through a synthetic rollback event

parameters.label: ^c20260807-67u

parameters.text: `Compaction.Event` is the `Session.Event.Tape` event that records a provider compacting a conversation-history region into continuation context

parameters.text: `Turn.Type` is the semantic role a referenced `Normal.Turn` plays at one typed relationship position within a `Chatlas.Line.Anchor.Dossier`

parameters.label: ^m2208-76b74b5c11c1bdb8
parameters.text: `Bloberia.Record` is the consumer's cargo, stored verbatim. There is no envelope: no id, no timestamps, no revision, no `value` wrapper.

parameters.label: ^m2208-598891bf572348e7
parameters.text: Bloberia never inspects cargo except at the paths a query names. Uniqueness, schema, collisions and meaning are consumer concerns.

parameters.label: ^m2208-a86adbe4ebb573e3
parameters.text: Arity belongs to the call, not to configuration: `first(query)` returns one match, `all(query)` returns every match. Nothing is declared and nothing is enforced.

parameters.label: ^m2208-8f6f64dd9f268e59
parameters.text: No configured primary key as a contract. A declared index is a cache hint only — addable, removable and repointable with no consequence for any consumer.

parameters.label: ^m2208-b371ce1a8ce9e29c
parameters.text: The storage filename is bloberia's private business. No consumer computes it, parses it, or holds it as a reference.

parameters.label: ^m2208-d63cfcca67532511
parameters.text: Refusing to model cargo is what lets one store serve consumers whose schemas move independently. A store that understands its cargo acquires a stake in every consumer's schema change.

parameters.label: ^m2208-36709b0ff81935a1
parameters.text: A `Depot.Type` is one storage topology under the shared contract — the way a library offers arrays, dicts and queues rather than one container.

parameters.label: ^m2208-4923f4ac5c00e360
parameters.text: The type belongs to the depot, is chosen at creation and recorded in its meta. A depot never mixes types.

parameters.label: ^m2208-601a74fc81e6d27c
parameters.text: `files` is the fully opaque type: one JSON document per record, demanding nothing of cargo.

parameters.label: ^m2208-b71cbb00948b909a
parameters.text: `shards` is the second type, taken from anchory's 2-hex design: many records per file, keyed by a declared cargo path. It exists because 3,956 records under `files` means 3,956 opens per scan.

parameters.label: ^m2208-76395e7cc62f555d
parameters.text: A type may add semantics of its own. Opacity is the `files` contract, not a property of bloberia as a whole — a consumer choosing `shards` opts into its terms, and a missing shard key is a loud failure rather than a silent one.

parameters.label: ^m2208-c239dd5b65d766df
parameters.text: Type-specific demands are depot configuration, declared at creation and recorded in meta; nothing is inferred from cargo.

parameters.label: ^m2208-5f3c996434853d93
parameters.text: Types stay substitutable only if the shared contract is fixed while implementations vary, so the API is settled now even though the type set grows.

parameters.label: ^m2208-b0e9402b205b4fd2
parameters.text: The failure mode is already demonstrated: two migration scripts in this project reimplemented anchory's 2-hex sharding because the layout leaked, which would have made anchory's storage unchangeable.

parameters.label: ^m2208-725b9f8ec26b3183
parameters.text: a `Bloberia.Depot` is one directory owning a `meta.json`, a `records/` tree, one lock and one git configuration.

parameters.label: ^m2208-849ead8a2990f16b
parameters.text: `~/Documents/bloberia` is a depot *root* holding many depots, not itself a depot. The three things that define the boundary — type, history, lock — are all per-depot, so the boundary cannot sit above them.

parameters.label: ^m2208-95c0997f35ba4ea4
parameters.text: a `Namespace` is placement inside a depot: same type, same history, same lock. The deciding question is whether the material needs its own storage type, its own history, or its own lifetime; if not, it is a namespace.

parameters.label: ^m2208-9193fdbc16c99d39
parameters.text: the git configuration is one path to the repo the depot's records live in, absolute or relative to `meta.json`. A depot may own its repo or sit inside one that already tracks it.

parameters.label: ^m2208-dfe2c7663fb0c3f0
parameters.text: a depot may own its repo or be tracked by an enclosing one; the index depot owns its own, because it lives user-side outside every project repo.

parameters.label: ^m2208-c97394d4ac78ef2c
parameters.text: the enclosing-repo case is real all the same: a depot placed inside a project must not nest a second `.git/` under it.

parameters.label: ^m2208-bc2b64cc256c8f28
parameters.text: A query names paths inside the cargo with `equals`, `contains` and `exists`, and bloberia iterates and matches.

parameters.label: ^m2208-454027766ae36514
parameters.text: Regex is not a first-round predicate. It is the one operator no index or prescan can serve, so admitting it now would guarantee a fast path and a slow path that diverge.

parameters.label: ^m2208-34e1ba305b3853bd
parameters.text: `contains` and `equals` are exactly the predicates `Scan.Decode.Verify` was designed to escalate through — cheap textual prescan, decode only candidates, verify against the parsed object.

parameters.label: ^m2208-79ea7c52062bf333
parameters.text: A declared index maps one cargo path to the records carrying each value, so a common lookup skips the scan.

parameters.label: ^m2208-88c426d2adf8b31f
parameters.text: An index is derived and disposable: droppable at any moment and rebuildable by full scan, exactly as `527` requires of a Normal Model cache.

parameters.label: ^m2208-5d9d574ebcc839ab
parameters.text: Staleness is detected, never assumed — an index carries a fingerprint of the depot state it was built from and rebuilds on mismatch.

parameters.label: ^m2208-27e97420ed211b99
parameters.text: A depot is rooted at an explicit directory, so placement is the caller's decision rather than bloberia's.

parameters.label: ^m2208-7b5c270ab891d277
parameters.text: The public depot root is `~/Documents/bloberia`, beside `~/Documents/chatlas`: an important system gets its own public home rather than hiding under a dotfile.

parameters.label: ^m2208-61beb7df8bdfa682
parameters.text: Every index record lives **user-side**, in one depot under `~/Documents/bloberia`. No index record is project-tier.

parameters.label: ^m2208-93556ba9c787ec03
parameters.text: A record's support points at chat evidence held in `~/Documents/chatlas`, which cannot ship with a project. Project-tier records would travel to a clone whose grounding resolves to nothing — storing them user-side does not create that problem, it stops pretending it is not there.

parameters.label: ^m2208-c64bbf917fd2512b
parameters.text: Reviewability survives the move: the user depot is its own repo, so a grounding change is still a diff. What is given up is atomicity with the markdown line, which two repos could never have enforced.

parameters.label: ^m2208-946e8cfb9a02439e
parameters.text: Placement legitimately differs per consumer — audience and lifetime differ — which is why one store must not impose one location.

parameters.label: ^m2208-59a8ce6a3e930072
parameters.text: The index is bloberia's first real consumer, and the thing that proves the design: one depot holds every index record, and anchory is retired into it.

parameters.label: ^m2208-c4c76166a685c315
parameters.text: Anchory is obsolete as a *design*, not as data. It holds 3,956 dossiers — essentially the whole grounding corpus — against 51 records that have made the trip. `index/record/store.py` already declares the merge in its own docstring; only the data is outstanding.

parameters.label: ^m2208-6371d951776590c7
parameters.text: The two shapes merge into one. `dossier: {app, attachment, relationships, schema}` and `record: {id, line, scope, trace, links, equivalence, schema}` describe the same fact through two generations; `LineRecord` is the survivor.

parameters.label: ^m2208-c2b4cf5c933aa041
parameters.text: Anchory's storage design survives its subsystem: the 2-hex shard becomes the `shards` depot type rather than being reimplemented a third time.

parameters.label: ^m2208-7c44ad8ec52b54e6
parameters.text: The two-tier logic dies with the move. `roots()`, tier moves in `put()` and `tier=` on every write all go; projects stay distinguishable because `scope.address` is already cargo, so it is a query rather than a namespace.

parameters.label: ^m2208-e024510c752cfb9e
parameters.text: Records keep their own identity: the index resolves through `line.label` and takes no `Record.Coordinate`.

parameters.label: ^m2208-94cc5737058c2ea8
parameters.text: a `Record.Coordinate` is `commit + file + path-in-file` — the full position of a value in git history, and the stable link the whole subsystem exists to provide.

parameters.label: ^m2208-54a8ad89f2a5fd41
parameters.text: it is derived on request, never allocated: bloberia stores no mapping and mints no id, so the reference costs no state and touches no cargo.

parameters.label: ^m2208-59a5abf1046c8625
parameters.text: it is read-side — obtained by asking about a record already in hand — so writing is unchanged and arity stays at the call.

parameters.label: ^m2208-771fd1ac54f8b817
parameters.text: an uncommitted record has no coordinate. Bloberia reports its absence and never fires a commit to manufacture one.

parameters.label: ^m2208-3cedc09f1b75d264
parameters.text: the path addresses sub-values, so a coordinate links to a piece of a record as readily as to the whole.

parameters.label: ^m2208-2b6628c7b4282a2d
parameters.text: git preserves each commit's tree as it was, so a coordinate keeps resolving across any later change of storage topology. The private layout and the permanent reference turn out to be compatible rather than opposed.

parameters.label: ^m2208-81d56ca33ac25d39
parameters.text: no bloberia-minted record id. A consumer that already has identity uses it: the index resolves through `line.label` and takes no coordinate.

parameters.label: ^m2208-06e76689ceb15fb4
parameters.text: `Stable.Surface` is a property of the surface a consumer builds, not a tier bloberia grants. A depot holding scratch and a depot holding index records differ in what the consumer promises, not in what the store does.

parameters.label: ^c20260630-0u

parameters.label: ^c20260510-1u
parameters.text: **Verified end to end on real data.** `first({"line.label": {"equals": ""}})` returns the `Stable.Surface` line with 6 support members, and its `Record.Coordinate` — `bloberia:06b9023…/records/bb.json#.line.body` — resolves out of the commit to the same text.

parameters.text: `Gr.Req` is the grounding-request artifact — a live note carrying one grounding campaign from discovery to landed links

parameters.text: structure: `Gr.Abstract` (target scope, coverage before/projected, status), `Gr.Set` (one entry per grounding target: anchor, evidence hint, why, landing form, status), `Gr.Log` (deviations, unattached anchors, drops with reasons)

parameters.label: ^m2208-4b45c557255d7952

parameters.label: ^m2208-f3b7672c544e7d5c

parameters.label: ^m2208-9bc6bfc79cfede9f

parameters.text: `Index.Appendix` is the appendix layer of the Index and the root concept for it — the on-demand depth, complement of `Index.Ontology`

parameters.label: ^m2208-677ba16aab415f25

parameters.label: ^c20260821-16u

parameters.text: `Block.Path` is a block name written as a `/`-separated path — the full path is the name

parameters.label: ^c20260712-80u

parameters.label: ^c20260712-27u

parameters.label: ^m2208-3db456d52609a71d

parameters.label: ^c20260712-38u

parameters.label: ^c20260712-86u

parameters.text: `Explicit.Namespace` is a concept whose purpose is to group a cluster of blocks — a declared view over the concepts it gathers

parameters.label: ^m2208-886f8cf66b5a14bf
parameters.text: its members are listed in `### meta` under `namespace-members` — the inventory of the cluster

parameters.label: ^m2208-cebc5c2707f3939e

parameters.label: ^m2208-e2ebe22121813be2

parameters.text: `Inline.Definition` is a `[DF]` line that defines a concept by inlining it inside another concept's block, without granting it a block of its own

parameters.label: ^c20260715-13u
parameters.text: the inline-defined name is a first-class `Named.Concept` — citable by `Dotted.Name` anywhere — but its truth lives on its host's line

parameters.label: ^c20260715-29u

parameters.label: ^c20260724-50u
parameters.text: every `Index.Depot` lives under a `Skw.Package` — it is that package's concept-store data structure, addressed by `Dotted.Name`

parameters.label: ^c20260724-79u

parameters.label: ^c20260722-35u
parameters.text: `Index.Depot.Dependency` is the index-addressing case of `Skw.Pkg.Dependency`: a depot resolves a `Dotted.Name` against another package's depot only through a declared dependency — package-visibility in the software sense

parameters.label: ^c20260722-40u

parameters.label: ^c20260722-27u

parameters.label: ^c20260722-28u

parameters.label: ^c20260722-30u
parameters.text: reachability and privilege are orthogonal — an `Index.Depot.Dependency` grants sight of another depot without ranking them, so it does not overturn "no depot privileged"

parameters.label: ^c20260719-46u
parameters.text: a `User.Gate` is an `Accountable.Assertion` whose claim is about the `Chat.Surface`: evidence of a declared kind can be found in the gated object's dossier

parameters.label: ^c20260719-30u
parameters.text: one declaration, two systems read it — **flow** (pre-evidence): the declaration shapes agent behavior before any evidence exists — stop, surface the thing, spend `User.Attention`, wait; runtime conversation control, honored in-session; **audit** (post-evidence): the recomputable assert over the dossier — checker territory, run any time, by anyone

parameters.label: ^c20260719-39u
parameters.text: the predicate family — existence: a turn of the declared `Turn.Type` is in the support set; correspondence: the turn's content matches the surface content; order: the evidence sequence is right — an approval that predates the current wording gates nothing

parameters.label: ^c20260719-24u

parameters.label: ^c20260719-23u

parameters.label: ^c20260719-51u
parameters.text: the robustness: enforcing the flow is hard; auditing it is cheap — the system does not prevent flow violations, it detects them and the gate invalidates retroactively; design for audit, not for enforcement

parameters.label: ^c20260719-27u
parameters.text: graded checkability: turn-exists, turn-typed, timestamp-order are CPU; "this turn really approves this content" is the agent floor

parameters.label: ^c20260719-25u

parameters.label: ^c20260716-67u
parameters.text: `Edition.Trigger.User.Gated` is the convenience gate: the user explicitly initiates the edit workflow — the agent never starts writing mid-conversation on its own

parameters.label: ^c20260716-70u

parameters.label: ^c20260716-48u

parameters.label: ^m2208-88e7ae5166f92dad
parameters.text: distinct from `Verbatim.User.Gated`, which gates what is written rather than when

parameters.text: `Verbatim.User.Gated` is a wording gate requiring presentation of materially equivalent content and later explicit user approval before that content is committed

parameters.text: the gate creates a deliberate `User.Attention` opportunity at the landing boundary

parameters.label: ^c20260729-171u
parameters.text: `Line.Verbatim.Gate` is its independently checkable per-`Index.Line` realization

parameters.label: ^c20260729-221u
parameters.text: one approval may cover several presented lines while each line retains its own gate evidence

parameters.label: ^c20260729-236u
parameters.text: the auditable predicate composes presentation, sufficient content correspondence, approval, and event order

parameters.label: ^c20260729-138u
parameters.text: sufficient correspondence does not require byte identity

parameters.label: ^c20260729-145u
parameters.text: the gate certifies protocol events rather than actual user cognition

parameters.label: ^c20260729-216u
parameters.text: it implies `Edition.Trigger.User.Gated` because explicit wording approval also approves the landing trigger

parameters.label: ^c20260729-356u
parameters.text: the system exposes proposed content while the user explicitly controls whether it may enter the gated surface

parameters.label: ^c20260729-74u
parameters.text: approval settles permission to land the presented wording; it does not certify factual truth

parameters.label: ^c20260725-123u
parameters.text: `Agentos.Daemon` is a single long-lived background process that runs registered `Background.Job`s, extending Agentos beyond one-shot CLI invocation

parameters.label: ^c20260725-108u
parameters.text: its process lifecycle is owned by the OS service manager (`launchd` on macOS) — start-at-login, keep-alive, and restart-on-crash come from the platform, not from hand-written daemonization

parameters.label: ^c20260725-106u
parameters.text: exactly one global instance runs per machine, making it the sole owner of background work and the sole writer of the shared state its jobs maintain

parameters.label: ^c20260725-121u
parameters.text: work reaches the daemon from two feeds — the internal scheduler firing jobs on their natural frequency, and external run-now triggers from the CLI (`Daemon.Trigger`)

parameters.label: ^c20260725-101u
parameters.text: both feeds converge on one serialized work lane: a single worker running one job to completion at a time

parameters.label: ^c20260725-117u
parameters.text: the single lane is what makes single-writer serialization and trigger coalescing fall out for free — without locks, a job queue, or async state

parameters.label: ^c20260725-115u
parameters.text: the daemon and the CLI are peer consumers of one core library; the daemon holds only scheduling and the trigger interface, never the work logic itself

parameters.label: ^c20260725-104u
parameters.text: each command is either daemon-path or CLI-local — exactly one path per command, chosen once

parameters.label: ^c20260725-175u
parameters.text: v1 adds no inline fallback when a daemon-path command finds the daemon down — dual-path redundancy is deferred, so daemon-path availability rests entirely on the service manager

parameters.label: ^c20260725-147u
parameters.text: concrete hosted jobs: continuous Chatlas index refresh over active sessions, and `Account.Management` rotation and usage monitoring — work that today runs only while a foreground command stays open

parameters.label: ^c20260725-124u
parameters.text: `Background.Job` is a named unit of recurring work an `Agentos.Daemon` hosts — a name, a natural frequency, and a `run()` body

parameters.label: ^c20260725-113u
parameters.text: the `run()` body lives in the core library — the same function the CLI would invoke directly — so the daemon carries scheduling, never a second copy of the work logic

parameters.label: ^c20260725-116u
parameters.text: the job registry is the shared interface between daemon and CLI: the daemon schedules jobs by it, the CLI names a job through it to trigger a run

parameters.label: ^c20260725-56u
parameters.text: a job must be safe to run more often than its natural frequency, because an external trigger can fire it between scheduled runs

parameters.label: ^c20260725-153u
parameters.text: a job stays incremental and cheap when nothing changed, so both frequent ticks and burst triggers stay affordable

parameters.label: ^c20260725-144u
parameters.text: Chatlas refresh is a job — each run re-ingests only sessions touched since the last run (`chatlas update --since`), keyed off recently active sessions detected at minute granularity

parameters.label: ^c20260725-125u
parameters.text: `Daemon.Trigger` is the interface by which a CLI force-runs a registered `Background.Job` now and receives its completion

parameters.label: ^c20260725-109u
parameters.text: its transport is a local unix domain socket — local-only, with filesystem permissions as the sole authorization; no TCP port or network surface

parameters.label: ^c20260725-118u
parameters.text: the submitting connection stays open for the request's lifetime and is at once the request, the wait, and the completion signal — one JSON line in, one JSON line out, then close

parameters.label: ^c20260725-100u
parameters.text: a trigger is satisfied by a job run that completes at or after the request moment; concurrent triggers arriving during one in-flight run all resolve off that single run (the coalescing rule)

parameters.label: ^c20260725-90u
parameters.text: the interface can fire only pre-registered jobs, never arbitrary operations — the trigger surface is the job registry, not remote code execution

parameters.label: ^c20260725-148u
parameters.text: failure detection falls out of the open connection: a daemon crash surfaces as EOF on the waiting read, and a CLI exit surfaces as a peer close to the daemon

parameters.label: ^m2208-ea1632d29585ed29

parameters.label: ^m2208-9b34f7c33f708777
parameters.text: `Grounding.Retrieval.Boundary` separates finding candidate evidence from linking it

parameters.label: ^m2208-e8e653233e882cff
parameters.text: retrieval quality affects linking quality, but retrieval mechanics are not the definition of grounding

parameters.label: ^m2208-fd2e702891e34f8b
parameters.text: search engines, vector databases, keyword indexes, and chatlas queries are candidate-discovery mechanisms

parameters.label: ^m2208-d1734f18f41a5bba
parameters.text: `Chat.Grounding.Target.Block` is the rule that chat grounding attaches to a kernel block, not to a loose topic

parameters.label: ^m2208-446e43758a2b8ee2
parameters.text: the index is the entity inventory that answers what is being grounded

parameters.label: ^m2208-24bebaed6fa91cf5
parameters.text: every chat grounding target is a `Index.Block` or `Appendix.Block`

parameters.label: ^m2208-0b6288667da4ec4d
parameters.text: if an issue or topic needs grounding, it must first resolve to an existing block or become a new block

parameters.label: ^m2208-14aaa7357eabb59c
parameters.text: if a subtopic inside a block needs independent grounding, it should become its own kernel block

parameters.label: ^m2208-89e96e7f1fc34728
parameters.text: a block's grounding is scoped to that one target block: its lines' anchors support its content only

parameters.label: ^m2208-5e781dd5c8c0c284
parameters.text: other surfaces cite grounded blocks instead of inventing separate grounding targets

parameters.label: ^m2208-5649d80a11a57c28
parameters.text: `Grounding.Hugentic.Authority` is the rule that grounding lines primarily anchor user turns

parameters.label: ^m2208-8a8950f6d62f45d1
parameters.text: assistant turns provide context, reasoning trace, proposed wording, and forensic evidence

parameters.label: ^m2208-656ae31206b678cc
parameters.text: assistant-authored material becomes normal grounding only when the user explicitly accepts, corrects toward, or acts on it

parameters.label: ^c20260708-9u
parameters.text: index grounding anchors target user turns only — gating guarantees an approval turn exists; there is no assistant-only index evidence

parameters.label: ^m2208-ec9c10b9d90623e9
parameters.text: grounding is a `Hugentic.Alignment` workflow: human/agent collaboration, not agent-only retrieval

parameters.label: ^c20260609-0u
parameters.text: `Designer.Turn.Kernel.Form` is how a `What.Design.Session` turn is shaped when working a defined subject

parameters.label: ^c20260609-1u
parameters.text: the designer communicates in `Kernel.Writing` — orthogonal bullet lines, each an independent fundamental point, direct language

parameters.label: ^c20260609-2u
parameters.text: a turn working a defined subject proposes a `Design.Block`: an H2 `Dotted.Notation` heading, orthogonal fundamentals, and an optional `### meta` for open items

parameters.label: ^c20260609-3u
parameters.text: a question turn pairs the block with the question — the `Design.Block` as actionable intro, then `Question / Why-now / Recommended-answer / Evidence`

parameters.label: ^c20260609-4u
parameters.text: every new question on a defined subject is accompanied by its block; pure openers are exempt because they create the first subject

parameters.label: ^c20260609-5u
parameters.text: discussion rounds re-render the same block with the change; open points live under `### meta` as `open:` lines

parameters.label: ^c20260609-6u
parameters.text: the in-chat block and the artifact's `Design.Index` block are one object — capture only adds gating

parameters.label: ^c20260609-7u
parameters.text: `RED.GREEN.Test.Suite` is the set of RED/GREEN-style tests an `Impl.Req` calls for, written test-first to drive the implementation

parameters.label: ^c20260609-8u
parameters.text: an `Impl.Exec` `Development.Principle`: the `Impl.Req` specifies the suite; the executer builds it test-first — each test goes RED (fails) then GREEN (minimal code passes), one at a time

parameters.label: ^c20260609-9u
parameters.text: never write all tests up front: bulk tests assert imagined shape and pass when behavior breaks

parameters.label: ^c20260609-10u
parameters.text: it is not the only tests — it is the implementation-driving core; more tests may be added later, including at the end

parameters.label: ^c20260609-11u
parameters.text: `No.Regression.Tests.Allowed` governs all tests including this suite — keep it core-feature, e2e, and durable-contract focused, not regression slop

parameters.label: ^c20260609-12u
parameters.text: `Test.At.Boundaries` governs what each test asserts — public behavior that survives a refactor

parameters.label: ^c20260609-13u
parameters.text: rationale: writing the test before the code prevents retrofit tests that merely rubber-stamp the implementation

parameters.label: ^m2208-579b09d17d0751b1
parameters.text: `QA.Space` is the implicit space of questions and possible answers that define a topic, artifact, task, source, or user model

parameters.label: ^m2208-ece1a17c513bcc87
parameters.text: alignment is the progressive conditioning of a `QA.Space` through agent/user interaction

parameters.label: ^m2208-3ad0d263b75d3d92
parameters.text: a `QA.Space` is a model, not a requirement that agents mechanically enumerate every question and answer

parameters.label: ^m2208-07360a6ff9798915
parameters.text: any state of a `QA.Space` can be described as answer regions that are open, constrained, fixed, touched, or untouched

parameters.label: ^m2208-c5b5a9ea22b156eb
parameters.text: the touched/open ratio is the control surface: the user tightens control by constraining more of the space, and delegates automation by leaving space open

parameters.label: ^m2208-c78525a7080c8b5f
parameters.text: hugentic surfaces nest over `QA.Space`: the `Chat.Surface` records it, the index digests it, and implementation surfaces realize it

parameters.label: ^m2208-f7b3f4c19ab7000b
parameters.text: `QA.Space` is never required complete to proceed; the agent works `Open.Space` to keep moving, and alignment catches up

parameters.label: ^c20260729-277u
parameters.text: `User.Model.Space` is a `QA.Space` about the user

parameters.label: ^c20260729-217u
parameters.text: it models what the system knows about what the user said, wanted, rejected, approved, left open, or delegated

parameters.label: ^c20260729-114u
parameters.text: its claims are evidence-scoped and belong only to the extent that a touched surface grounds them

parameters.label: ^c20260729-323u
parameters.text: `Hugentic.Chat.Surface` is its natural placement because repeated dialogue records changing judgment and context

parameters.label: ^c20260729-122u
parameters.text: non-chat `User.Touch` may also condition the model when its provenance is available

parameters.label: ^c20260729-335u
parameters.text: growing `Touched.Space` improves the user model by increasing its grounded interaction evidence

parameters.label: ^m2208-44d5aa8733718123
parameters.text: `Work.Space` is a `QA.Space` about the work at hand

parameters.label: ^m2208-7e6e4bd2819b9fc5
parameters.text: it models what is true, needed, selected, excluded, available, blocked, open, constrained, or fixed in the work

parameters.label: ^m2208-6bbd1b1900ef0552
parameters.text: agents act in the `Open.Space` of `Work.Space` and obey the `Constrained.Space` of `Work.Space`

parameters.label: ^m2208-914cf94f4e0e8223
parameters.text: touch is not an action gate for `Work.Space`; openness governs whether the agent decides

parameters.label: ^m2208-d892e61dc4a75312
parameters.text: `Source.Space` is a `QA.Space` about a source surface or source artifact

parameters.label: ^m2208-2871865e79d5afe5
parameters.text: it can model whatever matters about a source: what it says, contains, implies, connects to, supports, contradicts, enables, or raises as a point of interest

parameters.label: ^m2208-9c4c042ddd0cdf81
parameters.text: source-local signals do not by themselves establish current `User.Model.Space` claims unless they are grounded through a user-touched process

parameters.label: ^m2208-9fa1d1a26d6129bb
parameters.text: source surfaces feed alignment by surfacing candidate questions and points of interest for later touch

parameters.label: ^m2208-ebee33d92eb043ec
parameters.text: `Design.Space` is a `QA.Space` about artifact design

parameters.label: ^m2208-6472f97cd46758b7
parameters.text: it scopes `QA.Space` to design questions whose answers shape an artifact

parameters.label: ^m2208-657b801687e558d9
parameters.text: it is a vector space of `Design.Variable`s; each variable one axis, and `Design.Target.Model` is a point in this space

parameters.label: ^c20260729-279u
parameters.text: `User.Touched` is the property of data carrying evidence of `User.Touch`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-278u
parameters.text: `User.Touch` is an event in which the user engages a subject, providing the primitive evidence that the subject entered `Touched.Space`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-155u
parameters.text: the system does not observe `User.Touch` directly; it reaches touch only through its materialization on a `Touch.Authority.Surface`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-160u
parameters.text: touch is general over stated, discussed, approved, corrected, rejected, co-drafted, or explicitly delegated material

parameters.label: ^c20260729-198u
parameters.text: authorship is not the touch boundary: an agent may construct the data while its touch comes from user evidence

parameters.label: ^c20260729-52u
parameters.text: `User.Touched` separates `Touched.Space` from `Untouched.Space`; it does not decide whether a region is open, constrained, or fixed

parameters.label: ^c20260729-176u
parameters.text: `User.Touched` is derived per datum from touch provenance rather than stored as membership in a surface category

parameters.label: ^c20260729-268u
parameters.text: `Touch.Authority.Surface` is a registered surface that serves as an inbox for direct `Touched.Data`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-292u
parameters.text: a qualifying edition is a change that the surface recognizes as materializing `User.Touch`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-156u
parameters.text: the system observes qualifying surface editions, not the underlying `User.Touch` itself

parameters.label: ^c20260729-204u
parameters.text: data materialized by a qualifying edition is considered first-order `Touched.Data` by default

parameters.label: ^c20260729-102u
parameters.text: first-order touch classification is defeasible: later evidence may disqualify the edition or exclude particular data from its touched extent

parameters.label: ^c20260729-206u
parameters.text: each `Touch.Authority.Surface` defines which editions qualify and which data within them was touched

parameters.label: ^c20260729-129u
parameters.text: registration does not make every edition touched; a nonqualifying edition carries no direct touch

parameters.label: ^c20260729-87u
parameters.text: disqualification concerns touch provenance; factual error, staleness, or contradiction alone does not mean the data was never touched

parameters.label: ^c20260729-187u
parameters.text: a qualifying `User.Turn` is presently the only registered realization of `Touch.Authority.Surface`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-321u
parameters.text: `Chat.Surface` is the natural container and context surface for that realization

parameters.label: ^c20260729-270u
parameters.text: `Touched.Data` is data whose provenance reaches `User.Touch` through a qualifying `Touch.Authority.Surface` edition or through grounding

parameters.label: ^c20260729-205u
parameters.text: data materialized on the authority surface has defeasible first-order provenance; a grounded projection carries second-order provenance

parameters.label: ^c20260729-161u
parameters.text: touch provenance does not certify factual truth, internal consistency, or currentness

parameters.label: ^c20260729-357u
parameters.text: touched data conditions agent action according to what its evidence supports

parameters.label: ^m2208-12571868fa7bb472
parameters.text: `Touched.Space` is the region of a `QA.Space` carrying `User.Touched` evidence

parameters.label: ^m2208-ff3cef591725c8da
parameters.text: it is the part of the modeled space that the hugentic process has reached

parameters.label: ^m2208-ac0dcfa7e55e9147
parameters.text: the index is its primary alignment surface, but not the only one; the `Chat.Surface` is another hugentic surface that holds touch

parameters.label: ^m2208-fbdbc24298f7cd25
parameters.text: a touched region may be open or constrained; touch means engaged, not decided

parameters.label: ^m2208-6ab81d2d4bbd6c39
parameters.text: `Untouched.Space` is the region of a `QA.Space` with no `User.Touched` evidence

parameters.label: ^m2208-93408823d7b8d11e
parameters.text: it is the part of the modeled space the hugentic process has not reached

parameters.label: ^m2208-66a25f26ad5228f5
parameters.text: touch does not decide whether the agent may act; the `Open.Space` / `Constrained.Space` axis decides action

parameters.label: ^c20260716-63u
parameters.text: untouched material never becomes an index line directly; and touch alone lands nothing — material, touched or not, remains in chat, work surfaces, source surfaces, or `Index.Agendix` until landed through the gate

parameters.label: ^m2208-7b8dfa684d3401ad
parameters.text: alignment grows by moving important regions from `Untouched.Space` into `Touched.Space`

parameters.label: ^m2208-edd27b5cd694e4b5
parameters.text: `Open.Space` is the region of a `QA.Space` where meaningful agent choice remains

parameters.label: ^m2208-5632285a38911347
parameters.text: in `Open.Space`, the agent makes its own decisions to act: coherent, never random, and provisional

parameters.label: ^m2208-bf6cf03ebc29de74
parameters.text: `Open.Space` is orthogonal to touch: it may be untouched, or it may be touched by an explicit free declaration (`FR`)

parameters.label: ^m2208-c550bc319ea35be9
parameters.text: consequences logically entailed by constraints are not open; the agent may fail to derive them, but is not free to decide against them

parameters.label: ^m2208-6da7f6e2343dbb47
parameters.text: open resolutions become directive constraints only once touched

parameters.label: ^c20260729-262u
parameters.text: `Open.Inference` is an agent conclusion or decision made where applicable `Touched.Data` leaves the answer unresolved

parameters.label: ^c20260729-69u
parameters.text: an answer may remain unresolved because touched data is absent, incomplete, ambiguous, or contradictory

parameters.label: ^c20260729-234u
parameters.text: the agent evaluates provenance, applicability, currentness, support strength, and consequences before selecting an answer

parameters.label: ^c20260729-223u
parameters.text: open inference selects a coherent provisional action within the answer region left available by touched constraints

parameters.label: ^c20260729-115u
parameters.text: its conclusion carries no `Touched.Authority` of its own

parameters.label: ^c20260729-110u
parameters.text: it does not silently rewrite or discard touched positions that remain unresolved

parameters.label: ^c20260729-318u
parameters.text: the agent may act on open inference without waiting for additional `User.Touch`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-76u
parameters.text: changing a gated touched surface remains a separate reconciliation action even when open inference permits other work to proceed

parameters.label: ^m2208-1291af602f3b5570
parameters.text: `Constrained.Space` is the region of a `QA.Space` where possible answers have been narrowed below total freedom

parameters.label: ^m2208-fb4a4d45be930a6a
parameters.text: constraint can come from user directives, grounded arguments, formal implications, code reality, physical reality, or consequences of prior constraints

parameters.label: ^m2208-8dda897faf1adeb9
parameters.text: in `Constrained.Space`, the agent does not choose outside the remaining valid answer region

parameters.label: ^m2208-6775f661c13f8ea5
parameters.text: constraint strength varies; `Fixed.Space` is the maximally constrained endpoint

parameters.label: ^m2208-51762bd5eda97279
parameters.text: `Fixed.Space` is the region of `Constrained.Space` narrowed to one valid answer

parameters.label: ^m2208-02a93f8feb98b138
parameters.text: it is the 0%-free endpoint of the freedom axis

parameters.label: ^m2208-8d112af55792fbe2
parameters.text: a fixed region is not a decision point for the agent; the agent's job is to recognize and obey the fixed answer

parameters.label: ^c20260729-269u
parameters.text: `Touched.Authority` is the precedence rule by which `Touched.Data` conditions `Open.Inference` according to its provenance and meaning

parameters.label: ^c20260729-162u
parameters.text: touched authority is relative to `Open.Inference`; it is not a certificate of truth

parameters.label: ^c20260729-163u
parameters.text: touched data may be incomplete, stale, false, or mutually contradictory

parameters.label: ^c20260729-67u
parameters.text: an agent may not silently replace coherent touched data with its own `Open.Inference`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-68u
parameters.text: an agent must not blindly follow touched data whose applicable claims are incoherent

parameters.label: ^c20260729-210u
parameters.text: every `Touched.Surface` maintains a coherent live projection; detected incoherence is a `Point.Of.Interest`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-346u
parameters.text: resolution descends through provenance and may create new `User.Touch` while preserving the contradictory history

parameters.label: ^c20260729-197u
parameters.text: authority status is derived from provenance on the surface rather than stored

parameters.label: ^c20260729-271u
parameters.text: `Touched.Decision.Cycle` is the decision discipline repeated within product design and realization

parameters.label: ^c20260729-203u
parameters.text: contextualization loads the `Touched.Data` relevant to the active decision

parameters.label: ^c20260729-212u
parameters.text: incoherent touched constraints become `Point.Of.Interest` instances before they are treated as guidance

parameters.label: ^c20260729-79u
parameters.text: coherent touched constraints condition the valid answer region

parameters.label: ^c20260729-315u
parameters.text: regions not determined by touched constraints are completed through `Open.Inference`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-192u
parameters.text: action advances the current `Target.Product`

parameters.label: ^c20260729-225u
parameters.text: reconciliation compares the changed product with its touched design and adjacent surfaces

parameters.label: ^c20260729-342u
parameters.text: reconciliation may expose another decision and begin a nested cycle

parameters.label: ^c20260719-45u
parameters.text: `Constraint.Steering` is the design principle that we steer agent work by designing constraints — saturating surfaces with checkable assertions so that consistency pressure pulls the work in the designed direction

parameters.label: ^c20260719-29u
parameters.text: mint-time test: a finite vocabulary forces commitment at write time — confused content fails to type, the earliest and cheapest drift detection

parameters.label: ^c20260719-33u
parameters.text: standing test: the assertion rides next to the content forever; every later pass has a small, local, closed-set claim to check against

parameters.label: ^c20260719-26u
parameters.text: graded checkability: part of each assertion is CPU-checkable (presence, vocabulary membership, resolution), the rest agent-checkable — design pushes each assertion down the gradient; agent-checkable is the floor, never zero

parameters.label: ^c20260719-22u
parameters.text: direction-forcing: designing the constraint vocabulary IS steering the system — assertions encode what better looks like, so many small consistency checks pull the surfaces toward it

parameters.label: ^c20260719-32u
parameters.text: stability: an assertion is a semantic invariant a rewrite must preserve — constraints make a surface stable under agent rewriting; the agent may rephrase, never drop the pinned semantics

parameters.label: ^c20260719-50u
parameters.text: the compiler loop: agent-generated code must compile, and that feedback loop bounds generation — it either never converges or converges at least to compilable output; assertions + linting generalize the loop to text: the generated surface must comply with many tests, it is never "generate what you like"

parameters.label: ^c20260719-28u
parameters.text: instances: `Line.Type`, anchors + support sets (`Touched.Support.Network`), skw claims (`Skw.Ann.Dependency`), the annotation↔generated-surface sync (`Skw.Annotation`), gates, bless records

parameters.label: ^c20260719-47u
parameters.text: an `Accountable.Assertion` is the unit `Constraint.Steering` deposits: a recorded claim carrying frozen judgment (the stamp) and its audit path, so any agent can call it to account on demand

parameters.label: ^c20260719-18u
parameters.text: a stamp is judgment cached at mint time, never truth — checking recomputes the claim against its evidence

parameters.label: ^c20260719-42u
parameters.text: the trail has two realizations — integrated on-surface (for example an `Index.Line`'s type tag: evidence local to the value) or held in an external general schema (for example an `Anchory` dossier: audit requires descent); the axis between them is audit cost

parameters.label: ^c20260719-38u
parameters.text: the frozen judgment is someone's — user or agent — and the stamp says whose; accountability is the general property, authority stays read from provenance (`Touched.Authority`)

parameters.label: ^c20260720-44u

parameters.text: a `Tournament.Verdict` is the recorded outcome of one completed `Tournament.Match`

parameters.label: ^c20260805-72u
parameters.text: a verdict has two zones: an engine-written envelope and an opaque consumer slot, following `Bloberia.Record`

parameters.label: ^c20260806-53u~2
parameters.text: the envelope records the match identity, the judge, the ordering the judge returned, the presentation order actually run, and the `Match.Verbatim` hash

parameters.label: ^c20260809-43u

parameters.label: ^c20260809-106u

parameters.label: ^c20260805-74u
parameters.text: the engine stores the consumer slot and never reads it

parameters.label: ^c20260805-75u
parameters.text: slot content never shadows an envelope field; the slot carries analysis material, not a restatement of what the envelope owns

parameters.label: ^c20260806-54u~2
parameters.text: an outcome is either a strict total ordering of the match's players or `Tournament.Verdict::No.Contest`

parameters.label: ^c20260806-55u~3
parameters.text: the ordering is strict: a judge places no two players at equal rank, and equivalence emerges from orderings that disagree across repeated matches

parameters.label: ^c20260806-56u~2
parameters.text: pairwise comparisons are extracted from a stored ordering at read time and are never themselves stored

parameters.label: ^c20260806-57u~2
parameters.text: keeping the match whole is what leaves a later fold free to see which comparisons shared one judgment

parameters.label: ^c20260805-77u
parameters.text: there is no draw outcome; equally good players converge through split records across repeated matches

parameters.label: ^c20260805-78u
parameters.text: verdicts are append-only, and a later verdict never replaces an earlier one

parameters.label: ^c20260805-79u
parameters.text: one verdict is noise; signal lives only in accumulation

parameters.text: `Tournament.Verdict::No.Contest` is the outcome of a match its judge completed but declined to decide

parameters.label: ^c20260805-81u
parameters.text: it scores no player and enters no ranking fold

parameters.label: ^c20260806-60u~3

parameters.label: ^c20260805-83u

parameters.label: ^c20260805-84u

parameters.text: an `Improvement.Loop` is a `Run.Workspace` kind that spawns agents to raise a consumer-defined score over a subject, under consumer-defined constraints

parameters.label: ^c20260810-0u
parameters.text: one loop is three things: the `Mutable.Set` it may change, the `Loop.Constraint`s that must hold, and the `Loop.Score`s it is judged by

parameters.label: ^c20260810-1u
parameters.text: there is no loop engine — a loop is its definition and its own tooling, living in its workspaces

parameters.label: ^c20260810-2u
parameters.text: the improver changes only the `Mutable.Set`; everything outside it, the scorer and the constraints included, is fixed and may be understood but never altered

parameters.label: ^c20260810-3u
parameters.text: fixing everything outside the `Mutable.Set` prevents wasted execution rather than invalid results — a score is recomputable, so verification is the gate and the loop never has to be trusted

parameters.label: ^c20260809-101u
parameters.text: the workspace is the only writable surface, and the score reads its inputs from outside it

parameters.label: ^c20260810-4u
parameters.text: a `Loop.Constraint` may be mechanical or judged, and failing any of them zeroes the `Loop.Score` rather than trading against its other tests

parameters.label: ^c20260810-5u
parameters.text: a `Loop.Score` may be a vector of tests rather than one number; the improver is shown the results and reasons about the tradeoff itself

parameters.label: ^c20260810-6u
parameters.text: each candidate names its parent, so a loop's state lives in its lineage rather than in anything holding it

parameters.label: ^c20260809-102u
parameters.text: the product of a run is the read over its lineage: what was tried, what scored where, and what the best candidate changes

parameters.label: ^c20260810-7u
parameters.text: a disappointing run indicts exactly one of the three: no admitted candidate means the `Mutable.Set` is too narrow, a higher `Loop.Score` on worse work means a `Loop.Constraint` is missing, and no movement at all means the instrument did not discriminate

parameters.label: ^c20260810-8u
parameters.text: the `Loop.Constraint`s are the durable output: the improved subject is one artifact, while the constraint set is what the run taught about the subject

parameters.label: ^c20260810-9u
parameters.text: the domain stays consumer-owned: nothing interprets the subject, the score, or what an improvement is

parameters.label: ^c20260809-103u

parameters.label: ^c20260810-10u
parameters.text: nothing judges whether a score measures anything — a badly chosen metric produces clean iterations and an empty reading

parameters.text: `Agentos.Hook` is the named event ingress and dispatch mechanism through which producers invoke registered Agentos subsystem callbacks.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-4u
parameters.text: Hook names are dot-separated, namespaced identifiers whose first segment identifies the owning domain.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-5u
parameters.text: Subsystems register zero or more callbacks under an exact hook name during Agentos CLI composition.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-6u
parameters.text: The dispatcher invokes every callback registered under the received hook name sequentially in registration order.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-7u
parameters.text: A callback failure is logged and dispatch continues with the remaining callbacks.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-8u
parameters.text: Callback failures do not fail the hook command; invocation validation failures do.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-9u
parameters.text: Failure logs identify the hook and callback without recording the complete context by default.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-10u
parameters.text: Initial registration excludes wildcard subscriptions, priorities, dynamic discovery, and dependency ordering.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-11u
parameters.text: Callback return values and response aggregation remain undefined until a consumer requires them.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-12u
parameters.text: `Agentos.Hook.Invocation` is the value delivered to the dispatcher, composed of a hook `name`, an optional `ctx_type`, and a JSON-object `ctx`.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-13u
parameters.text: `ctx` remains opaque to the dispatcher and is passed unchanged to each selected callback.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-14u
parameters.text: `ctx_type` is an optional open-string label identifying the context producer or schema; its absence means unknown or untyped context.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-15u
parameters.text: `ctx_type` accompanies `ctx` without being inserted into it and does not participate in callback selection.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-16u
parameters.text: The public ingress command is `agentos hook --name <hook-name> [--ctx-type <ctx-type>]`.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-17u
parameters.text: Each CLI invocation selects exactly one context input: `--ctx-from-stdin` or `--ctx <json>`.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-18u
parameters.text: `--ctx-from-stdin` is the canonical harness input and reads the JSON context from standard input.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-19u
parameters.text: `--ctx <json>` is the inline input for small manual invocations.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-20u
parameters.text: Malformed JSON, a missing hook name, or conflicting context inputs invalidate the invocation before dispatch.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-21u
parameters.text: `Agent.Hook` is the initial agent-lifecycle vocabulary within the general `Agentos.Hook` namespace.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-22u
parameters.text: An agent provider integration maps its native lifecycle callbacks onto the nearest matching `Agent.Hook` names.

parameters.label: ^c20260811-23u

parameters.label: ^c20260720-29u
parameters.text: **One block shape**: `$kw: [address] [--flags]` opens; `$kw. end` closes a content block. The **address is optional and orthogonal** — a block may be nameless or named, and naming never changes how it closes. `$kw` marks the fence, `--` fills it (head line *and* belonging lines carry flags, each self-marked by `--`); the sigil appears only on the fence lines.

parameters.label: ^c20260720-29u~2
parameters.text: **Composition — a body is native surface text and/or nested blocks**. A `Semantic.Router` is a named block whose children are nameless `--when`/`--then` rows, each carrying a **native-text body** (the situation / the resource — real surface text, never a flag value).

parameters.label: ^c20260720-30u
parameters.text: **Closure is by role, not by naming — three cases**  :

parameters.label: ^c20260720-29u~3
parameters.text: **[DC] the structural layer resolves to composition, not flags** — the parser today has *two* layers: an annotation layer (`text`/`copy`/`derived`/`depends`) and a structural layer (`router`/`when`/`then`, with peer-closure + router-row alternation). v2 maps both onto the one block shape: `text` → a fenced body with no binding; `copy`/`derived`/`depends` → `--copy`/`--derived`/`--from`; **`router`/`when`/`then` → a named block whose children are nameless `--when`/`--then` rows with native-text bodies**; `label` → a `^`-addressed span. Closure is role-based (content owns `end`, rows peer-close), which *shrinks* the parser: the peer-closure registry, router-child stack tracking, and `end-when`/`end-then` all collapse into "`--when`/`--then` alternate inside a router."

That collapse is a **pure internal-representation refactor with no acceptance-signal impact** — no acceptance signal names `SkwBlock`; all name the v2 *grammar*, the v2 POI set, package parity, and the real note. Executing the collapse would force a full rewrite of `build.py`'s consumer layer (`recipe.verb`/`body_span`/`recipe_key`/`.recipes`/`.constructs`/`.dependencies`/`_emit` masking) **and** the 1500-line test suite's structural assertions, multiplying the blast radius of an already-breaking change. **Chosen faithful path**: implement the full v2 *grammar* over the existing typed-construct output — the parser maps `--derived`/`--copy`→recipe verb, `--from`-only→dependency, fenced-no-binding→`text` construct, `--when`/`--then`→nested rows under a router-parent — so `build.py` stays mostly *additive* (new POIs + note storage). The recursive `SkwBlock` is deferred as a later no-behavior refactor. Every acceptance signal is still met; the primary intent (grammar) is delivered in full. Blast radius: `model.py` grammar surface + `build.py` additive POIs + test grammar-literal updates + 28-file machinery migration.

parameters.label: ^c20260721-1u~2
parameters.text: 2026-07-20 — **closure rule completed to three cases + `--to` reserved, folded in** (``): the v2-vs-all-4-skills survey found two forms the two-case closure did not yet cover — the void `depends` one-liner and the `--to` flag (teaching-text only). Resolved in chat: closure has **three** roles, not two — (1) materializing blocks (`--derived`/`--copy`/`text`) own a **mandatory** `end`; (2) a router owns an `end` and its `--when`/`--then` rows peer-close; (3) **declaration-only blocks** (`--from`/`--note`/`--supp`/`--intent` only) **self-close** with no `end`, subsuming void `depends` and pure-note attach. Writing an `end` is the author's opt-in from attach-by-address into fence-the-body; materializing blocks have no choice. `--to` is carried as a **reserved, unused** flag (parsed and preserved, no linter behavior). Every current agentos-index / 4-skill form now maps to v2 with no ambiguity. No open grammar hole remains for Phase 1.
